Chapter 13: Living with Intention and Aligning with Values
When you think about what really brings lasting happiness, it’s not just chasing after quick wins or doing what everyone else expects. True, lasting joy comes from living in alignment with your own values and intentions—making choices that actually reflect what matters most to you, instead of just reacting on autopilot or getting swept along by outside pressures.
Living with intention is kind of like steering your own boat. Rather than drifting along with the current, you’re choosing your direction. But to do that, you need clarity—about your values, your priorities, and your goals.
So, how do you start living more intentionally? Here are a few key steps that can help:
First, get clear on your core values. Maybe you value honesty, kindness, creativity, or growth. Everyone’s list is a little different, so take some time and really ask yourself what feels true for you.
Next, set goals that actually reflect those values—not just what looks impressive on paper, or what other people say you should want. For example, if creativity is central to you, maybe you sign up for an art class, or carve out time for writing every week.
Another important step? Regularly check in with yourself. Ask, “Is this choice aligned with what matters most to me?” It’s a simple question, but it can really shift your perspective—and help you say yes to what lights you up, and no to what doesn’t.
And remember, you don’t have to stick to a rigid plan. Sometimes, you’ll need to adjust your course—and that’s totally okay. Flexibility and self-compassion are key.
Let’s say your core value is connection. You might decide to spend more time with family or friends, even if it means turning down other demands. Or, if you really value learning, you might seek out new experiences or challenges that help you grow.
Intentional living isn’t about perfection or ticking every box. It’s about making conscious choices—practicing self-reflection, honesty, and a bit of courage along the way.
Over time, as you keep coming back to what really matters, you’ll start to notice more purpose and fulfillment in your life. You’ll find it easier to let go of habits that don’t serve you, and invest your energy in what truly counts.
So, as you move forward, try steering your own boat. Check in with your values, make choices that align, and give yourself permission to adjust as you go. That’s where a deeper sense of happiness really begins.
